events.text: The declaration search found no existing relative Picard degree transformation. It did confirm the intended target and universal property are already present: mathlib’s `continuousMapPresheafAb ℤ` and the project’s `PicSharp.etaleSheafHomEquiv`. The substantive missing construction is therefore objectwise degree on arbitrary line-bundle families and proof it respects the relative quotient, addition, and pullback; I’m reading those exact quotient and sheaf interfaces now.

     9	/-!
    10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
    11	
    12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
    13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
    14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
    15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
    16	
    17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
    18	
    19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
    20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
    21	a sheaf** (Kleiman §2, L1330: "not *a priori* a sheaf"), and over a general
    22	field it is **not representable** — the witness is Exercise `ex:Pfs`, the conic
    23	`u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ`, smooth proper geometrically integral with no rational
    24	point.
    25	
    26	**CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`).** This paragraph asserted
    27	non-sheafness "not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302)",
    28	and glossed it as: a line bundle can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T`
    29	without being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`. Both the citation and the gloss are
    30	wrong. L1292–L1302 proves that the **absolute** functor `Pic_X` is never a
    31	separated Zariski presheaf, using `T = ℙ¹_X`; the quotient by `π_T^* Pic(T)`
    32	that defines the *relative* functor is exactly what kills that argument, and
    33	L1600–L1605 in fact proves `Pic_{X/S} ≅ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` when `f` has a section.
    34	Sheafifying is still the right move and the conclusion below is unaffected —
    35	only the stated reason was. Full account in
    36	`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`'s module docstring.
    37	
    38	Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
    39	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
    40	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
    41	hypothesis.
    42	
    43	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
    44	supplied:
    45	
    46	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
    47	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
    48	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
    49	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
    50	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
    51	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
    52	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
    53	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
    54	
    55	## The site
    56	
    57	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
    58	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
    59	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
    60	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
    61	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
    62	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
    63	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
    64	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
    65	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
    66	hypothesis.
    67	
    68	## Main definitions
    69	
    70	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
    71	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
    72	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
    73	  relative Picard presheaf.
    74	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
    75	  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
    76	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
    77	  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
    78	  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
    79	  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
    80	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
    81	  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
    82	  must match.
    83	
    84	## References
    85	
    86	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
    87	étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
    88	Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
    89	`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.
    90	-/

   104	/-- **The étale topology on `(Sch/k)`.**
   105	
   106	The big étale topology on schemes (`Scheme.etaleTopology`, Mathlib
   107	`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`) localised at `Spec k` along SGA 4
   108	III 5.2.1 (`GrothendieckTopology.over`): a sieve of a `k`-scheme `T` is
   109	covering exactly when the sieve it generates on the underlying scheme
   110	`T.left` is covering for the étale topology
   111	(`GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff`).

   130	*stronger* than sheafifying Zariski-locally: a Zariski sheaf need not be an

   133	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ≤ etaleTopologyOver k := by
   134	  intro T S hS
   135	  rw [GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff] at hS ⊢
   136	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology _ hS

   140	/-! ## §2. The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor -/
   141	
   142	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor** `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`
   143	(Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, étale-sheaf clause).
   144	
   145	The associated étale sheaf of the relative Picard presheaf
   146	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), as a bundled object
   147	of `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`. Its sheaf property is not an
   148	assumption but part of the datum — `Sheaf.cond`, extracted as
   149	`etaleSheaf_isSheaf` below — which is the whole point of passing to it: the
   150	unsheafified `relPresheaf` is not *a priori* an étale sheaf (Kleiman §2 L1330),
   151	so representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is the statement one can ask for over an
   152	arbitrary field.
   153	
   154	**Corrected 2026-07-30 (`review-ajc`): this said "not a sheaf even
   155	Zariski-locally", and that is the withdrawn claim.** It is wrong about exactly
   156	the functor named here. The lines it derives from (Kleiman §2 L1292–L1302) prove
   157	that the **absolute** `Pic_X` is never a separated Zariski presheaf; the
   158	**relative** functor — `relPresheaf`, this one — is *defined* by quotienting out
   159	`Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that argument. On these binders `th:cmp` part 1
   160	gives the opposite direction *in Kleiman*, `Pic_{X/S} ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` whenever
   161	`O_S = f_*O_X` universally, i.e. `relPresheaf` is Zariski-**separated** there.
   162	
   163	**That last clause is about the SOURCE, and the Lean name first cited here does
   164	not carry it** (`review-ajc`, corrected in the same session by a fresh-context
   165	audit of this very fix). `PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy`
   166	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) takes a `rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X`
   167	hypothesis and concludes the Zariski sheaf property *from representability*, by
   168	subcanonicity — the converse direction, conditional on exactly what the seam
   169	lacks. `PicEtSubcanonical`'s §4 docstring scopes it correctly as "only the first
   170	half"; that caveat was dropped in copying the citation here. **Nothing in this
   171	project proves `th:cmp` part 1.**
   172	
   173	The seam and the blueprint were both corrected
   174	for this on 2026-07-29 (`I-0970`, `I-0973`) and this site was missed. Do not
   175	restore a Zariski-sheaf reason here; take the non-representability directly, via
   176	`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`, whose one open input is

   178	
   179	This is a genuine instantiation of the parametric `PicSharp.etSheaf` of
   180	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` at the canonical étale topology, with one
   181	correction: `etSheaf` sheafifies the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`
   182	(`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)`), whereas Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and the
   183	representability theorem are about the *relative* one, `relPresheaf`. It is
   184	the relative functor that is sheafified here.

   186	The abelian-group structure survives sheafification because the target
   187	`AddCommGrpCat` has the sheafification adjunction
   188	(`HasWeakSheafify` for a concrete, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful
   189	functor); `toEtaleSheaf` below is the unit. -/

   199	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
   200	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
   201	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
   202	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
   203	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
   204	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
   205	
   206	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/

   208	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :

   243	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
   244	
   245	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
   246	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
   247	forgotten,
   248	
   249	```
   250	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
   251	```
   252	
   253	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
   254	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda

  1223	/-! ## §2. The Abel map — line-bundle / Quot correspondence
  1224	
  1225	The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
  1226	map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
  1227	`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
  1228	`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.
  1229	
  1230	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
  1231	Def. `dfn:Abel` + Thm. `th:repDiv`). -/
  1232	
  1233	/-! ### The Abel map
  1234	
  1235	The class `HasAbelMap` carries the map itself (a data field `abel`), so that
  1236	`abelMap` has the defining property `abelMap_app_mk` below; the instance
  1237	supplies the explicit natural transformation `abelMapWitness C`.
  1238	
  1239	Construction of `abelMapWitness C : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)]`:
  1240	a relative effective divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` on `C ×_k T` has invertible ideal
  1241	`I_D = ker q`; the Abel map sends its class to
  1242	`[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[I_D]`, the additive inverse (in the group-valued target
  1243	`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`) of the class of the ideal sheaf.  It is assembled as the
  1244	composite `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, where `abelKernelNatTrans` is the
  1245	substantive `[D] ↦ [I_D]` transformation and `picNeg` is the (natural)
  1246	negation on the group-valued functor.
  1247	
  1248	Naturality of `abelKernelNatTrans` is the mathematical heart: for a test map
  1249	`g : T' ⟶ T` the base-change square is cartesian (`quotBaseSquare`), and the
  1250	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
  1251	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose
  1252	side hypotheses — epi `q`, quasi-coherent source, finitely-presented `F`,
  1253	`T`-flat `F`, invertible kernel — are exactly the fields of `DivFamily`), so
  1254	`ker` commutes with base change and the class `[ker q]` is natural.  Negation
  1255	is natural because `Pic^♯`'s pullback maps are group homomorphisms.
  1256	
  1257	The `dual` route (`Modules.dual (ker q)` as an explicit inverse) is available
  1258	for the *object-level* invertibility (`dual_isLocallyTrivial`) but is not used
  1259	here: the group-inverse `-[ker q]` is the canonical `[I_D⁻¹]` and makes
  1260	naturality rest only on the kernel–pullback comparison, avoiding the
  1261	not-yet-formalised sheaf-level dual-pullback commutation.
  1262

300	/-! ## §1b. The relative Picard `H_T`-coset setoid
   301	
   302	`PicSharp.addCommGroup` lives on `Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT)`,
   303	whose carrier setoid is the **iso-class** relation `Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)` — i.e. the
   304	**absolute** `Pic(C ×_S T)`. The blueprint (`lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, Kleiman §2 `df:Pfs`) asks
   305	instead for the **relative** quotient `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)`, the quotient by the subgroup
   306	`H_T := im π_T^*`. This section builds that quotient directly as a coarser setoid
   307	`relPicSetoid` on `LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT`, together with the abelian-group instance
   308	`PicSharp.addCommGroup_via_tensorObj` on it.
   309	
   310	**Relation (multiplicative form).** For `L L' : OnProduct πC πT` set
   311	```
   312	L ~ L'   ↔   ∃ N locally trivial on T,  L.carrier ≅ π_T^* N ⊗ L'.carrier,
   313	```
   314	where `π_T^* N = (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier`. This is the left-coset
   315	relation of `H_T := im π_T^*`. It is **equivalent** to the blueprint's `L ⊗ L'^{-1} ≅ π_T^* N`
   316	(tensor both sides by `L'` / its inverse), but the multiplicative form avoids naming the tensor
   317	inverse of `L'` in the *definition* — only the setoid-symmetry step consumes a tensor inverse (of
   318	`N` on the base `T`, via `Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`). The blueprint statements
   319	`lem:relpic_setoid_{refl,symm,trans}`, `lem:relpic_add_welldef` and `lem:pullback_inverse_iso`
   320	are realized below in that multiplicative form. -/
   321	
   322	/-- **The `H_T`-coset relation on `OnProduct πC πT`** (relative Picard, multiplicative form):
   323	`L ~ L' ↔ ∃ N loc-triv on T, L.carrier ≅ π_T^* N ⊗ L'.carrier`. It encodes the
   324	quotient `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` of `lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, and is coarser than the
   325	absolute iso-class relation `RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup`. -/
   326	def relPicRel {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S)
   327	    (L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) : Prop :=
   328	  ∃ (N : T.Modules) (hN : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial N),
   329	    Nonempty (L.carrier ≅
   330	      Modules.tensorObj (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier L'.carrier)
   331	
   332	/-- An isomorphism of the underlying bundles implies the `H_T`-coset relation (take `N = 𝒪_T`):
   333	the relative relation is coarser than the absolute iso-class relation. Used to
   334	transport the abelian-group axioms from the absolute iso-class group. -/
   335	theorem relPicRel_of_iso {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
   336	    {L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT} (e : Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)) :
   337	    relPicRel πC πT L L' := by
   338	  obtain ⟨e⟩ := e
   339	  refine ⟨SheafOfModules.unit T.ringCatSheaf, isLocallyTrivial_unit, ⟨?_⟩⟩
   340	  exact e ≪≫ (Modules.tensorObj_left_unitor L'.carrier).symm ≪≫
   341	    Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Modules.pullbackUnitIso (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).symm
   342	      (Iso.refl L'.carrier)
   343	
   344	/-- **Reflexivity of the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_refl`): `L ~ L`, witnessed
   345	by `N = 𝒪_T` and the pullback–unit iso `π_T^* 𝒪_T ≅ 𝒪_{C×T}` plus the left unitor. -/
   346	theorem relPicRel_refl {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S)
   347	    (L : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) : relPicRel πC πT L L :=
   348	  relPicRel_of_iso ⟨Iso.refl _⟩
   349	
   350	/-- **Symmetry of the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_symm`): from `L ~ L'` (via `N`)
   351	get `L' ~ L` (via the tensor inverse `N⁻¹` on `T`), using multiplicativity of `π_T^*`, the
   352	pullback–unit iso, and `Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`. -/
   353	theorem relPicRel_symm {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
   354	    {L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT} (h : relPicRel πC πT L L') :
   355	    relPicRel πC πT L' L := by
   356	  obtain ⟨N, hN, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
   357	  obtain ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨eN⟩⟩ := Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse hN
   358	  refine ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨?_⟩⟩
   359	  -- `tensorObj (π_T^*Ninv) L ≅ L'`, then take `.symm`.
   360	  refine Iso.symm ?_
   361	  refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl _) e ≪≫ ?_
   362	  refine (Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso
   363	    (M := (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier)

   559	/-! ## §3. Functoriality (group-homomorphism strengthening)

   561	The naturality lemma `RelPicPresheaf.functorial` produces, for

   567	both sides, this set map upgrades to an additive-monoid homomorphism

   570	sides; the upgrade is the substantive content of

   574	consumes `functorial` as its morphism action.)

300	/-! ## §1b. The relative Picard `H_T`-coset setoid
   301	
   302	`PicSharp.addCommGroup` lives on `Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT)`,
   303	whose carrier setoid is the **iso-class** relation `Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)` — i.e. the
   304	**absolute** `Pic(C ×_S T)`. The blueprint (`lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, Kleiman §2 `df:Pfs`) asks
   305	instead for the **relative** quotient `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)`, the quotient by the subgroup
   306	`H_T := im π_T^*`. This section builds that quotient directly as a coarser setoid
   307	`relPicSetoid` on `LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT`, together with the abelian-group instance
   308	`PicSharp.addCommGroup_via_tensorObj` on it.
   309	
   310	**Relation (multiplicative form).** For `L L' : OnProduct πC πT` set
   311	```
   312	L ~ L'   ↔   ∃ N locally trivial on T,  L.carrier ≅ π_T^* N ⊗ L'.carrier,
   313	```
   314	where `π_T^* N = (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier`. This is the left-coset
   315	relation of `H_T := im π_T^*`. It is **equivalent** to the blueprint's `L ⊗ L'^{-1} ≅ π_T^* N`
   316	(tensor both sides by `L'` / its inverse), but the multiplicative form avoids naming the tensor
   317	inverse of `L'` in the *definition* — only the setoid-symmetry step consumes a tensor inverse (of
   318	`N` on the base `T`, via `Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`). The blueprint statements
   319	`lem:relpic_setoid_{refl,symm,trans}`, `lem:relpic_add_welldef` and `lem:pullback_inverse_iso`
   320	are realized below in that multiplicative form. -/
   321	
   322	/-- **The `H_T`-coset relation on `OnProduct πC πT`** (relative Picard, multiplicative form):
   323	`L ~ L' ↔ ∃ N loc-triv on T, L.carrier ≅ π_T^* N ⊗ L'.carrier`. It encodes the
   324	quotient `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` of `lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, and is coarser than the
   325	absolute iso-class relation `RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup`. -/
   326	def relPicRel {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S)
   327	    (L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) : Prop :=
   328	  ∃ (N : T.Modules) (hN : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial N),
   329	    Nonempty (L.carrier ≅
   330	      Modules.tensorObj (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier L'.carrier)
   331	
   332	/-- An isomorphism of the underlying bundles implies the `H_T`-coset relation (take `N = 𝒪_T`):
   333	the relative relation is coarser than the absolute iso-class relation. Used to
   334	transport the abelian-group axioms from the absolute iso-class group. -/
   335	theorem relPicRel_of_iso {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
   336	    {L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT} (e : Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)) :
   337	    relPicRel πC πT L L' := by
   338	  obtain ⟨e⟩ := e
   339	  refine ⟨SheafOfModules.unit T.ringCatSheaf, isLocallyTrivial_unit, ⟨?_⟩⟩
   340	  exact e ≪≫ (Modules.tensorObj_left_unitor L'.carrier).symm ≪≫
   341	    Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Modules.pullbackUnitIso (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).symm
   342	      (Iso.refl L'.carrier)
   343	
   344	/-- **Reflexivity of the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_refl`): `L ~ L`, witnessed
   345	by `N = 𝒪_T` and the pullback–unit iso `π_T^* 𝒪_T ≅ 𝒪_{C×T}` plus the left unitor. -/
   346	theorem relPicRel_refl {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S)
   347	    (L : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) : relPicRel πC πT L L :=
   348	  relPicRel_of_iso ⟨Iso.refl _⟩
   349	
   350	/-- **Symmetry of the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_symm`): from `L ~ L'` (via `N`)
   351	get `L' ~ L` (via the tensor inverse `N⁻¹` on `T`), using multiplicativity of `π_T^*`, the
   352	pullback–unit iso, and `Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`. -/
   353	theorem relPicRel_symm {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
   354	    {L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT} (h : relPicRel πC πT L L') :
   355	    relPicRel πC πT L' L := by
   356	  obtain ⟨N, hN, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
   357	  obtain ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨eN⟩⟩ := Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse hN
   358	  refine ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨?_⟩⟩
   359	  -- `tensorObj (π_T^*Ninv) L ≅ L'`, then take `.symm`.
   360	  refine Iso.symm ?_
   361	  refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl _) e ≪≫ ?_
   362	  refine (Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso
   363	    (M := (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier)
   364	    (N := (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier) (P := L'.carrier)).symm ≪≫ ?_
   365	  refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
   366	    (Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT) Ninv N hNinv hN).symm
   367	    (Iso.refl L'.carrier) ≪≫ ?_
   368	  refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
   369	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).mapIso
   370	      (Modules.tensorObj_braiding Ninv N ≪≫ eN)) (Iso.refl L'.carrier) ≪≫ ?_
   371	  exact Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Modules.pullbackUnitIso (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT))
   372	    (Iso.refl L'.carrier) ≪≫ Modules.tensorObj_left_unitor L'.carrier
   373	
   374	/-- **Transitivity of the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_trans`): from `L ~ L'` (via
   375	`N`) and `L' ~ L''` (via `N'`) get `L ~ L''` via `N ⊗ N'`, using the associator and
   376	multiplicativity of `π_T^*`. -/
   377	theorem relPicRel_trans {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
   378	    {L L' L'' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT}
   379	    (h : relPicRel πC πT L L') (h' : relPicRel πC πT L' L'') :
   380	    relPicRel πC πT L L'' := by
   381	  obtain ⟨N, hN, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
   382	  obtain ⟨N', hN', ⟨e'⟩⟩ := h'
   383	  refine ⟨Modules.tensorObj N N', Modules.tensorObj_isLocallyTrivial hN hN', ⟨?_⟩⟩
   384	  refine e ≪≫ Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl _) e' ≪≫ ?_
   385	  refine (Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso
   386	    (M := (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier)
   387	    (N := (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N' hN').carrier) (P := L''.carrier)).symm ≪≫ ?_
   388	  exact Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
   389	    (Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT) N N' hN hN').symm
   390	    (Iso.refl L''.carrier)
   391	
   392	/-- **The relative Picard carrier setoid** `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` (blueprint
   393	`lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, carrier), the `H_T`-coset relation on `LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT`.
   394	This is the RELATIVE quotient, distinct from the absolute iso-class
   395	setoid `RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup`. -/
   396	def relPicSetoid {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) :
   397	    Setoid (LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) where
   398	  r := relPicRel πC πT
   399	  iseqv := ⟨relPicRel_refl πC πT, relPicRel_symm, relPicRel_trans⟩
   400	
   401	/-- **The middle-four interchange for `⊗`** `(A ⊗ B) ⊗ (C ⊗ D) ≅ (A ⊗ C) ⊗ (B ⊗ D)`, assembled from
   402	the associator and the braiding. Helper for `relPicRel_add`. -/
   403	private noncomputable def tensorMiddleFour {X : Scheme.{u}} (A B C D : X.Modules) :
   404	    Modules.tensorObj (Modules.tensorObj A B) (Modules.tensorObj C D) ≅
   405	      Modules.tensorObj (Modules.tensorObj A C) (Modules.tensorObj B D) :=
   406	  Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso ≪≫
   407	    Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl A)
   408	      (Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso (M := B) (N := C) (P := D)).symm ≪≫
   409	    Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl A)
   410	      (Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Modules.tensorObj_braiding B C) (Iso.refl D)) ≪≫
   411	    Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl A)
   412	      (Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso (M := C) (N := B) (P := D)) ≪≫
   413	    (Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso (M := A) (N := C) (P := Modules.tensorObj B D)).symm
   414	
   415	/-- **Addition is well defined on the `H_T`-quotient** (blueprint `lem:relpic_add_welldef`): if
   416	`L₁ ~ L₂` and `L₁' ~ L₂'` then `L₁ ⊗ L₁' ~ L₂ ⊗ L₂'`, via the middle-four interchange and
   417	multiplicativity of `π_T^*`. -/
   418	theorem relPicRel_add {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
   419	    {L₁ L₂ L₁' L₂' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT}
   420	    (h : relPicRel πC πT L₁ L₂) (h' : relPicRel πC πT L₁' L₂') :
   421	    relPicRel πC πT (Modules.tensorObjOnProduct πC πT L₁ L₁')
   422	      (Modules.tensorObjOnProduct πC πT L₂ L₂') := by
   423	  obtain ⟨N, hN, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
   424	  obtain ⟨N', hN', ⟨e'⟩⟩ := h'
   425	  refine ⟨Modules.tensorObj N N', Modules.tensorObj_isLocallyTrivial hN hN', ⟨?_⟩⟩
   426	  -- `L₁ ⊗ L₁' ≅ (π_T^*N ⊗ L₂) ⊗ (π_T^*N' ⊗ L₂')`.
   427	  refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso e e' ≪≫ ?_
   428	  -- middle-four → `(π_T^*N ⊗ π_T^*N') ⊗ (L₂ ⊗ L₂')`.
   429	  refine tensorMiddleFour (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier L₂.carrier
   430	    (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N' hN').carrier L₂'.carrier ≪≫ ?_
   431	  -- multiplicativity of `π_T^*`: `π_T^*N ⊗ π_T^*N' ≅ π_T^*(N ⊗ N')`.
   432	  exact Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
   433	    (Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT) N N' hN hN').symm
   434	    (Iso.refl (Modules.tensorObj L₂.carrier L₂'.carrier))
   435	
   436	/-- The chosen tensor-inverse of `L` as an element of `OnProduct πC πT`, via
   437	`Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`; it underlies negation on the relative Picard
   438	quotient. -/
   439	private noncomputable def relNegOnProduct {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
   440	    (L : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT :=
   441	  ⟨Classical.choose (Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse L.isLocallyTrivial),
   442	    (Classical.choose_spec (Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse L.isLocallyTrivial)).1⟩
   443	
   444	/-- **Negation is compatible with the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_symm`, negation
   445	form): if `L ~ M` then their chosen tensor-inverses satisfy `L⁻¹ ~ M⁻¹`. The witness is `N⁻¹` on the
   446	base `T`; both inverses are tensor-inverses of `L`, so they agree up to iso by `pInverseUnique`. -/

   450	  obtain ⟨N, hN, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
   451	  obtain ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨eN⟩⟩ := Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse hN

   453	  have hLinv : Modules.tensorObj L.carrier (relNegOnProduct L).carrier ≅

   456	  have hMinv : Modules.tensorObj M.carrier (relNegOnProduct M).carrier ≅
   457	      SheafOfModules.unit (Limits.pullback πC πT).ringCatSheaf :=
   458	    (Classical.choose_spec (Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse M.isLocallyTrivial)).2.some
   459	  have hOther : Modules.tensorObj L.carrier
   460	      (Modules.tensorObj (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier
   461	        (relNegOnProduct M).carrier) ≅
   462	      SheafOfModules.unit (Limits.pullback πC πT).ringCatSheaf := by
   463	    refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso e (Iso.refl _) ≪≫ ?_
   464	    refine tensorMiddleFour (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier M.carrier
   465	      (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier
   466	      (relNegOnProduct M).carrier ≪≫ ?_
   467	    refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
   468	      (Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial
   469	        (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT) N Ninv hN hNinv).symm hMinv ≪≫ ?_
   470	    refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
   471	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).mapIso eN) (Iso.refl _) ≪≫ ?_
   472	    refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Modules.pullbackUnitIso (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT))
   473	      (Iso.refl _) ≪≫ ?_
   474	    exact Modules.tensorObj_left_unitor _

   477	/-- Descended addition on the relative Picard quotient: `[L] + [L'] := [L ⊗ L']`, well-defined by
   478	`relPicRel_add`. -/
   479	private noncomputable def relAddVia {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S} :

   483	    (fun L L' => Quotient.mk _ (Modules.tensorObjOnProduct πC πT L L'))

    94	/-! ## §1. Line bundles on a product
    95	
    96	A *line bundle* on the relative curve `C ×_S T` is an invertible
    97	`O_(C ×_S T)`-module, i.e. a sheaf of modules locally free of rank one. In
    98	Mathlib `b80f227` the `Scheme.Modules` category is in place
    99	(`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf`), but there is no `IsInvertible`
   100	predicate on its objects yet (the closest is `Module.Invertible R M` for rings,
   101	in `Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup`). iter-187 supplies the missing
   102	predicate as a project-side definition via local trivialisation on an affine
   103	open cover (see `IsLocallyTrivial` below), and refines `OnProduct` to the
   104	corresponding subtype.
   105	
   106	Blueprint reference: `def:line_bundle_on_product` (Kleiman §2, "absolute Picard
   107	functor"; Stacks tag 01HK). -/
   108	
   109	/-- A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `M` is **locally trivial of rank one** if every
   110	point `x : X` has an affine open neighbourhood `U` on which the restriction
   111	`M|_U` is isomorphic to the structure sheaf-as-module `𝒪_U`. This is the
   112	project-side stand-in for the missing Mathlib `IsInvertible` predicate on
   113	`Scheme.Modules`: line bundles (invertible sheaves) are exactly the
   114	`IsLocallyTrivial` modules, by Stacks tag 01HK / Hartshorne II §6. Local
   115	trivialisability is the structural content that survives base change along
   116	`f : Y ⟶ X` (Stacks 01HH) and is the source of the invertibility-preservation
   117	step for `pullbackAlongProjection`.
   118	
   119	The witness is bundled as `Nonempty (M.restrict U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.unit _)`:
   120	the existence of a sheaf-of-modules isomorphism over the affine chart. -/
   121	def IsLocallyTrivial {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules) : Prop :=
   122	  ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧
   123	    Nonempty (M.restrict U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.unit (U : Scheme).ringCatSheaf)
   124	
   125	/-- The type of **line bundles on the product** `C ×_S T`: invertible sheaves of
   126	`O_(C ×_S T)`-modules, where the product is the categorical pullback of the
   127	projections `πC : C ⟶ S` and `πT : T ⟶ S`. In Kleiman's notation with `X = C`
   128	and base `S`, this is `Pic_C(T) = Pic(C ×_S T)`, the value of the absolute
   129	Picard functor at `T`.
   130	
   131	iter-187: refined to the subtype of `(Limits.pullback πC πT).Modules` cut out
   132	by the project-side predicate `IsLocallyTrivial` (locally trivial of rank one).
   133	The carrier is now genuinely the line-bundle subobject of `Scheme.Modules`,
   134	matching the blueprint statement `def:line_bundle_on_product`. Iter-186's
   135	all-modules carrier is recovered by forgetting the second component. -/
   136	def OnProduct {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) : Type (u+1) :=
   137	  { M : (Limits.pullback πC πT).Modules // IsLocallyTrivial M }
   138	
   139	/-- Projection from a line bundle on the product to its underlying
   140	sheaf of modules. -/
   141	abbrev OnProduct.carrier {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
   142	    (L : OnProduct πC πT) : (Limits.pullback πC πT).Modules := L.1
   143	
   144	/-- A line bundle on the product is locally trivial of rank one. -/
   145	lemma OnProduct.isLocallyTrivial {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
   146	    (L : OnProduct πC πT) : IsLocallyTrivial L.carrier := L.2
   147	
   148	/-- **Stacks 01HH (pullback of an invertible sheaf is invertible).** For any
   149	morphism of schemes `f : Y ⟶ X` and any locally-trivial sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules
   150	`M`, the pulled-back module `f^* M : Y.Modules` is again locally trivial.
   151	
   152	The proof unfolds an affine open cover trivialising `M`, pulls back along `f`,
   153	and observes that `f^*` commutes with restriction along open immersions (the
   154	`pullback`/`restrictFunctor` natural isomorphism in
   155	`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf`) so that the trivialising chart for
   156	`M|_U` becomes a trivialising chart for `(f^* M)|_(f⁻¹ U)`. The full chart-chase
   157	involves the natural-isomorphism `restrictFunctorIsoPullback` plus the
   158	preservation of `SheafOfModules.unit` under pullback (Mathlib
   159	`Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.PullbackFree`'s
   160	`unitToPushforwardObjUnit`). The chart-chase is complete and the lemma is
   161	proved below. -/
   162	lemma IsLocallyTrivial.pullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) {M : X.Modules}
   163	    (hM : IsLocallyTrivial M) :
   164	    IsLocallyTrivial ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj M) := by
   165	  intro y
   166	  obtain ⟨U, hxU, hU_aff, eM⟩ := hM (f.base y)
   167	  have hyU' : y ∈ f ⁻¹ᵁ U := hxU
   168	  obtain ⟨V, hV_aff, hyV, hVU⟩ := exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset hyU'
   169	  refine ⟨V, hyV, hV_aff, ?_⟩
   170	  -- Stacks 01HH chart-chase: factor `V.ι ≫ f` through `U` using
   171	  -- `Scheme.Hom.resLE`, then transport through `restrictFunctorIsoPullback`
   172	  -- and `pullbackComp` to identify the pullback at `V` with the pullback of
   173	  -- the unit on `U` to `V`. Close via `eM` and `pullbackObjUnitToUnit`
   174	  -- (which is an iso since `Opens.map g.base` is final via the
   175	  -- `RepresentablyFlat` instance).
   176	  obtain ⟨eM⟩ := eM
   177	  set g : (V : Scheme) ⟶ (U : Scheme) := f.resLE U V hVU with hg_def
   178	  have hg_comp : g ≫ U.ι = V.ι ≫ f := Scheme.Hom.resLE_comp_ι f hVU
   179	  haveI : (TopologicalSpace.Opens.map g.base).Final :=
   180	    CategoryTheory.final_of_representablyFlat _
   181	  refine ⟨?_⟩
   182	  -- 1: ((pullback f).obj M).restrict V.ι ≅ (pullback V.ι).obj ((pullback f).obj M)
   183	  let i1 :=
   184	    (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback V.ι).app ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj M)
   185	  -- 2: ≅ (pullback (V.ι ≫ f)).obj M
   186	  let i2 := (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp V.ι f).app M
   187	  -- 3: ≅ (pullback (g ≫ U.ι)).obj M  (using V.ι ≫ f = g ≫ U.ι)
   188	  let i3 := (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr hg_comp.symm).app M
   189	  -- 4: ≅ (pullback g).obj ((pullback U.ι).obj M)
   190	  let i4 := ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g U.ι).symm).app M

   201	/-! ## §2. The pullback functor along the projection
   202	
   203	For a morphism of schemes `f : Y ⟶ Z` and an invertible `O_Z`-module `M`, the
   204	pullback `f^* M` is an invertible `O_Y`-module (the pullback of an
   205	open-cover-trivialisation of `M` trivialises `f^* M`, and the pullback of a free
   206	module of rank one is free of rank one — Stacks tag 01HH). Specialising to the
   207	projection `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT : C ×_S T ⟶ T` gives the pullback map
   208	`π_T^* : Pic(T) → Pic(C ×_S T)`. Mathlib's underlying `Scheme.Modules.pullback`
   209	functor (in `Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf`) supplies the pullback on
   210	the full category of sheaves of modules; iter-175+ will restrict it to
   211	invertible sheaves once the `OnProduct` carrier is unpacked.

   214	01HH). -/

   217	curve. Sends a *line bundle on `T`* — i.e. an `O_T`-module `N` equipped with a
   218	proof `hN : IsLocallyTrivial N` — to the line bundle `π_T^* N` on `C ×_S T`,

   225	locally-trivial witness comes from the project-side helper
   226	`IsLocallyTrivial.pullback` (Stacks 01HH), which is proved. -/
   227	noncomputable def pullbackAlongProjection {S C T : Scheme.{u}}

   229	    OnProduct πC πT :=

   233	/-! ## §3. Composition of pullbacks
   234	
   235	The composition law for line-bundle pullback (Stacks tag 01HG) says that for any
   236	composable morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y, g : Y ⟶ Z` and any line bundle `M ∈ Pic(Z)`,
   237	the natural isomorphism `(g ∘ f)^* M ≅ f^* g^* M` makes the pullback functor
   238	into a (pseudo-)functor `Sch^op ⥤ Cat`.
   239	
   240	Specialised to the relative curve setting: given `g : T' ⟶ T` over `S`, the
   241	base-change morphism `g_C := id_C ×_S g : C ×_S T' ⟶ C ×_S T` satisfies
   242	`π_T ∘ g_C = g ∘ π_{T'}` (definition of the fiber product). Therefore on
   243	line bundles `g_C^* ∘ π_T^* = π_{T'}^* ∘ g^*`, with the equality realised as the
   244	canonical natural isomorphism of pullback functors via the pseudo-functoriality
   245	of `Scheme.Modules.pullback` (Mathlib `Modules.pullbackComp`).
   246	
   247	Blueprint reference: `lem:pullback_compose` (Kleiman §2; Stacks tag 01HG). -/
   248	
   249	/-- **Composition of line-bundle pullbacks** along the projection. For a base
   250	scheme `S`, a curve-side morphism `πC : C ⟶ S`, test objects `T, T'` over `S`
   251	via `πT : T ⟶ S` and `πT' : T' ⟶ S`, and a morphism `g : T' ⟶ T` over `S`
   252	(encoded by the hypothesis `πT' = g ≫ πT`), set
   253	`g_C := id_C ×_S g : C ×_S T' ⟶ C ×_S T`
   254	(the base-change morphism, given by `pullback.map`). On the underlying
   255	`Scheme.Modules.pullback` functors the two routes through the canonical
   256	naturality square give canonically isomorphic objects:
   257	```
   258	            Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd πC πT)
   259	  T.Modules  ─────────────────────────────────────────────►  (C ×_S T).Modules
   260	       │                                                              │
   261	       │ Scheme.Modules.pullback g            Scheme.Modules.pullback g_C
   262	       ▼                                                              ▼
   263	 T'.Modules  ─────────────────────────────────────────────►  (C ×_S T').Modules
   264	            Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd πC πT')
   265	```
   266	i.e. for any `N : T.Modules`,
   267	```
   268	(Modules.pullback g_C).obj ((Modules.pullback (pullback.snd πC πT)).obj N)
   269	  ≅
   270	(Modules.pullback (pullback.snd πC πT')).obj ((Modules.pullback g).obj N).
   271	```
   272	
   273	This natural isomorphism is the substantive content of the
   274	"line-bundle pullback functor is well-behaved under composition" fact
   275	(Stacks tag 01HG). At the level of the `OnProduct` carrier (which is a typed
   276	`sorry` in iter-174; see §1) it descends to equality of isomorphism classes
   277	`[g_C^* π_T^* N] = [π_{T'}^* g^* N] ∈ OnProduct πC πT'`.
   278	
   279	iter-186: closed via the chain
   280	1. `Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g_C (pullback.snd πC πT)` (functor iso applied at `N`)
   281	2. `Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr` for the equation `g_C ≫ snd πC πT = snd πC πT' ≫ g`
   282	   (`pullback.lift_snd` on the `pullback.map` lift).
   283	3. `(Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (pullback.snd πC πT') g).symm` (applied at `N`). -/
   284	theorem pullback_pullback_eq {S C T T' : Scheme.{u}}
   285	    (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) (πT' : T' ⟶ S) (g : T' ⟶ T)
   286	    (hg : πT' = g ≫ πT) (N : T.Modules) :
   287	    Nonempty
   288	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
   289	            (Limits.pullback.map πC πT' πC πT (𝟙 C) g (𝟙 S)
   290	              (by rw [Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]) (by rw [Category.comp_id, hg]))).obj
   291	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).obj N) ≅
   292	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT')).obj
   293	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj N)) := by
   294	  set g_C : Limits.pullback πC πT' ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT :=
   295	    Limits.pullback.map πC πT' πC πT (𝟙 C) g (𝟙 S)
   296	      (by rw [Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]) (by rw [Category.comp_id, hg])
   297	  have key : g_C ≫ Limits.pullback.snd πC πT = Limits.pullback.snd πC πT' ≫ g :=
   298	    Limits.pullback.lift_snd _ _ _
   299	  refine ⟨?_⟩
   300	  refine (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g_C (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).app N ≪≫ ?_
   301	  refine (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr key).app N ≪≫ ?_
   302	  exact ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT') g).app N).symm
   303	
   304	end LineBundle

   308	/-! ## §4. The relative Picard quotient (set-valued)
   309	
   310	The relative Picard presheaf `Pic^♯_{C/S}(T) := Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)`
   311	quotients the line-bundle group of the product by the subgroup pulled back from
   312	the base. As a quotient of abelian groups it is a quotient set; equivalently,
   313	the equivalence relation `L ~ L' ↔ L ⊗ L'⁻¹ ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)` is captured by a
   314	`Setoid` on the line-bundle type `OnProduct πC πT`. The quotient
   315	`Quotient (preimage_subgroup πC πT)` is the underlying set of the relative
   316	Picard presheaf at `T`.
   317	
   318	The "preimage_subgroup" name follows the Kleiman/Stacks convention: the
   319	quotient is by the preimage `π_T^* Pic(T) ⊆ Pic(C ×_S T)`, treated as a
   320	subgroup (image of a group homomorphism); the project-side Lean encoding
   321	extracts the *Setoid* that the quotient construction takes.
   322	
   323	Blueprint reference: `thm:relative_pic_quotient_well_defined` (Kleiman §2,
   324	Def. `df:Pfs`). -/
   325	
   326	/-- **Well-definedness of the relative Picard quotient as a `Setoid`.**
   327	
   328	The equivalence relation on `OnProduct πC πT` defining the relative Picard
   329	presheaf
   330	```
   331	Pic^♯_{C/S}(T) := Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)
   332	```
   333	is the relation `L ~ L' ↔ L ⊗ L'⁻¹ ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)`. This relation is reflexive
   334	(`L ⊗ L⁻¹ = O_(C ×_S T) = π_T^* O_T ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)`), symmetric (the inverse of
   335	a line bundle in `π_T^* Pic(T)` is in `π_T^* Pic(T)`), and transitive
   336	(`L ⊗ L'⁻¹ ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)` and `L' ⊗ L''⁻¹ ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)` give
   337	`L ⊗ L''⁻¹ ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)`); hence is an equivalence relation, encoded by a
   338	`Setoid` on `OnProduct πC πT`.
   339	
   340	The substantive content is the well-definedness of the quotient: the canonical
   341	projection `OnProduct πC πT → Quotient (preimage_subgroup πC πT)` is the
   342	set-theoretic underlying map of the relative Picard presheaf at `T`.
   343	
   344	iter-186: with `OnProduct := (pullback πC πT).Modules`, the carrier is the
   345	modules category. We encode the **iso-class setoid** `L ~ L' ↔ Nonempty (L ≅ L')`.
   346	This is a substantive simplification: it identifies isomorphic modules
   347	(giving the underlying set of `Pic(C ×_S T)` once invertibility is imposed),
   348	but does not yet quotient by the pullback subgroup `π_T^* Pic(T)`. The full
   349	quotient requires a tensor-product structure on `Scheme.Modules` (Mathlib
   350	ships `PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` but no monoidal structure on
   351	`Scheme.Modules` directly at `b80f227`) plus an inverse for invertibles;
   352	iter-187+: refine to `L ~ L' ↔ ∃ N : T.Modules, Nonempty (L ⊗ L'⁻¹ ≅
   353	pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N)` once both are available. -/
   354	noncomputable def preimage_subgroup {S C T : Scheme.{u}}
   355	    (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) :
   356	    Setoid (LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) where
   357	  r L L' := Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)
   358	  iseqv :=
   359	    { refl := fun _ => ⟨Iso.refl _⟩
   360	      symm := fun ⟨e⟩ => ⟨e.symm⟩
   361	      trans := fun ⟨e₁⟩ ⟨e₂⟩ => ⟨e₁ ≪≫ e₂⟩ }
   362	
   363	/-! ## §5. Naturality in the test scheme — the relative Picard presheaf as a functor
   364	
   365	For a morphism `g : T' ⟶ T` over `S` (encoded by the equality `πT' = g ≫ πT`),
   366	the base-change `g_C := id_C ×_S g : C ×_S T' ⟶ C ×_S T` induces a map
   367	`g_C^* : Pic(C ×_S T) → Pic(C ×_S T')` on line bundles, which (by
   368	`lem:pullback_compose` = `pullback_pullback_eq` above) sends the subgroup
   369	`π_T^* Pic(T)` into `π_{T'}^* Pic(T')`. Therefore it descends to a unique map
   370	on quotients
   371	```
   372	g^♯ : Pic^♯_{C/S}(T) ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/S}(T'),    [L] ↦ [g_C^* L],
   373	```
   374	making `Pic^♯_{C/S} : (Sch/S)^op ⥤ Set` a presheaf.

   379	`map_id`, `map_comp` fields) is iter-175+ work once `OnProduct` and the
   380	`preimage_subgroup` carrier are unpacked.

    24

    41	  retraction is bijective.  The `ℤ[T]` input is

    43	  dehomogenisation argument over an arbitrary commutative base ring.
    44	
    45	  `Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Topology.lean` turns "both chart rings are
    46	  domains" into integrality: reducedness by `IsReduced.of_openCover`, and
    47	  irreducibility because the (nonempty) overlap is a dense irreducible subset
    48	  of each chart, hence of their union.

     8	/-!
     9	# The support of a finite module commutes with base change
    10	
    11	`AJC.picrep.divzero`, carrier bridge (a).
    12	
    13	This file proves the **carrier identity** the divisor-side reduction of
    14	`Picard/DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean` was missing: for a finite `A`-module `M` and
    15	an `A`-algebra `B`, the support of the base change `B ⊗[A] M` is the contraction
    16	preimage of the support of `M`,
    17	
    18	```
    19	Supp_B (B ⊗[A] M) = (Spec B → Spec A)⁻¹ (Supp_A M).
    20	```
    21	
    22	The pointwise form `support_baseChange_finite` is the workhorse; the set equality
    23	`support_baseChange_finite_eq` and the emptiness corollaries package it for the
    24	two consuming directions.
    25	
    26	## Why this is the bridge, and not a re-spelling
    27	
    28	`Picard/QuotSupportBaseChange.lean` already proves the *forward* ideal-sheaf
    29	inclusion `annihilator F ≤ (annihilator (g'^* F)).map g'`, which yields
    30	`supp (g'^* F) ⊆ g'⁻¹ (supp F)` — properness of the *larger* support and nothing
    31	more. The identification of the two carriers appearing in
    32	`Scheme.DivFamily.isFinite_support_of_fibers` (the **support of the fibre**
    33	`schematicSupport (fiberModule …)` versus the **fibre of the support**) needs the
    34	*reverse* inclusion `g'⁻¹ (supp F) ⊆ supp (g'^* F)`, which is exactly what the
    35	reverse direction of `support_baseChange_finite` supplies. It is a genuine
    36	theorem, not a vocabulary rotation on the annihilator: it changes the containing
    37	set from `supp F` to `supp (g'^* F)`, which `rfl` does not identify.
    38	
    39	## Proof
    40	
    41	At a prime `q : Spec B` with contraction `p = comap q`, membership in the support
    42	of a finite module is nontriviality of the residue-field fibre
    43	(`Module.mem_support_iff_nontrivial_residueField_tensorProduct`). Three canonical
    44	identifications close it:
    45	
    46	1. `κ(q) ⊗[B] (B ⊗[A] M) ≃ₗ[κ(q)] κ(q) ⊗[A] M` — base-change cancellation
    47	   (`TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange`).
    48	2. `κ(q) ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[κ(q)] κ(q) ⊗[κ(p)] (κ(p) ⊗[A] M)` — the same cancellation
    49	   through the residue-field extension `κ(p) → κ(q)`
    50	   (`Ideal.ResidueField.map`, which exists because `p = q.comap (algebraMap A B)`),
    51	   with the scalar tower `A → κ(p) → κ(q)` supplied by
    52	   `Ideal.ResidueField.map_algebraMap`.
    53	3. `Nontrivial (κ(q) ⊗[κ(p)] N) ↔ Nontrivial N` — a field extension is faithfully
    54	   flat (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.nontrivial_tensorProduct_iff_right`).
    55	
    56	No noetherian, flatness, or finite-presentation hypothesis on `M` beyond
    57	`Module.Finite` (needed only so that support is a closed set of primes and the
    58	residue-field criterion applies).
    59	
    60	## References
    61	
    62	* [Stacks, Tag 056J] (support and base change); [Stacks, Tag 05DR].
    63	* Mathlib: `Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalRing/Module.lean`
    64	  (`Module.mem_support_iff_nontrivial_residueField_tensorProduct`),
    65	  `Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat/Basic.lean`.
    66	-/
    67	
    68	set_option autoImplicit false
    69	
    70	open TensorProduct
    71	
    72	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    73	
    74	universe u
    75	
    76	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    77	
    78	/-- **Support commutes with base change** (finite module, pointwise form). For a
    79	finite `A`-module `M` and an `A`-algebra `B`, a prime `q` of `B` lies in the
    80	support of the base change `B ⊗[A] M` if and only if its contraction
    81	`comap q` lies in the support of `M`.
    82	
    83	The reverse implication `comap q ∈ Supp M → q ∈ Supp (B ⊗ M)` is the inclusion
    84	`g'⁻¹ (supp F) ⊆ supp (g'^* F)` that `Picard/QuotSupportBaseChange.lean`'s
    85	forward annihilator inclusion does not provide, and is the carrier bridge (a)
    86	of `Scheme.DivFamily.isFinite_support_of_fibers`. No flatness hypothesis. -/
    87	theorem support_baseChange_finite (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    88	    [Module.Finite A M] (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    89	    q ∈ Module.support B (B ⊗[A] M) ↔
    90	      PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B) q ∈ Module.support A M := by
    91	  set p := PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B) q with hp
    92	  rw [Module.mem_support_iff_nontrivial_residueField_tensorProduct,
    93	      Module.mem_support_iff_nontrivial_residueField_tensorProduct]
    94	  -- the residue-field extension `κ(p) → κ(q)`, from `p = q.comap (algebraMap A B)`
    95	  have hcom : p.asIdeal = q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap A B) := rfl
    96	  letI φ : p.asIdeal.ResidueField →+* q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
    97	    Ideal.ResidueField.map p.asIdeal q.asIdeal (algebraMap A B) hcom
    98	  letI algφ : Algebra p.asIdeal.ResidueField q.asIdeal.ResidueField := φ.toAlgebra
    99	  haveI htower : IsScalarTower A p.asIdeal.ResidueField q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
   100	    apply IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq
   101	    intro a
   102	    change (algebraMap A q.asIdeal.ResidueField) a = φ _
   103	    rw [Ideal.ResidueField.map_algebraMap,
   104	        IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply A B q.asIdeal.ResidueField]
   105	  -- 1. cancel the `B`-base change: `κ(q) ⊗[B] (B ⊗[A] M) ≃ κ(q) ⊗[A] M`
   106	  have e1 : Nontrivial (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[B] (B ⊗[A] M))
   107	      ↔ Nontrivial (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M) :=
   108	    (AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A B q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   109	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField M).toEquiv.nontrivial_congr
   110	  -- 2. re-expand through `κ(p)`: `κ(q) ⊗[A] M ≃ κ(q) ⊗[κ(p)] (κ(p) ⊗[A] M)`
   111	  have e2 : Nontrivial (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M)
   112	      ↔ Nontrivial (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[p.asIdeal.ResidueField]
   113	          (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M)) :=
   114	    ((AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   115	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField q.asIdeal.ResidueField M).toEquiv.nontrivial_congr).symm
   116	  -- 3. `κ(q)` is faithfully flat over the field `κ(p)`
   117	  have e3 : Nontrivial (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[p.asIdeal.ResidueField]
   118	        (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M))
   119	      ↔ Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M) :=
   120	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.nontrivial_tensorProduct_iff_right
   121	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   122	  rw [e1, e2, e3]
   123	
   124	/-- **Support commutes with base change** (finite module, set-equality form): the
   125	support of `B ⊗[A] M` is the contraction preimage of the support of `M`. -/
   126	theorem support_baseChange_finite_eq (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
   127	    [Module.Finite A M] :
   128	    Module.support B (B ⊗[A] M)
   129	      = PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B) ⁻¹' Module.support A M := by
   130	  ext q
   131	  simpa using support_baseChange_finite M q
   132	
   133	/-- The base change `B ⊗[A] M` of a finite module has **empty support exactly on the
   134	primes lying over the support of `M`**; in particular if `Supp_A M = ∅` then
   135	`Supp_B (B ⊗[A] M) = ∅`. The direction actually consumed by the divisor-side
   136	reduction: emptiness of every fibre-of-support is emptiness of every
   137	support-of-fibre. -/
   138	theorem support_baseChange_finite_eq_empty_of_isEmpty (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M]
   139	    [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M] (h : Module.support A M = ∅) :
   140	    Module.support B (B ⊗[A] M) = ∅ := by
   141	  rw [support_baseChange_finite_eq, h, Set.preimage_empty]
   142	
   143	end AlgebraicGeometry
